source.text: וִֽירִיחוֹ֙ סֹגֶ֣רֶת וּמְסֻגֶּ֔רֶת מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֵ֥ין יוֹצֵ֖א וְאֵ֥ין בָּֽא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And Jericho [was] shutting up and shut up because of [the] sons of Israel; none going out and none coming in.

en.L: Now Jericho was shutting itself up and was shut up because of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; no one was going out and no one was coming in.
en.B: Now Jericho was shut up tight because of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Nobody left the city and nobody entered it.
en.R: The gates of Jericho were shut and barred because the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were near. No one went out of the city, and no one came in.

decisions.choice: shutting up and shut up: closed tight
decisions.reason: The same verb comes twice, first active and then passive: the city shut itself and was kept shut. Together they say it was closed completely, with no way in or out, as the end of the verse spells out.

decisions.choice: Now Jericho ...: a pause that sets the scene
decisions.reason: The verse breaks off the story to describe the city. It stands between the meeting with the commander of the LORD's army (5:13-15) and the LORD's words to Joshua (verse 2), and shows what Israel faced: a walled city that would not come out to fight or open its gates.

decisions.choice: Jericho: a walled city in the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: Jericho stood west of the Jordan, not far from Israel's camp at Gilgal (4:19; 5:10). Its people had already heard what the LORD had done for Israel and were afraid (2:9-11; 5:1).

decisions.choice: The gates ... were shut and barred; because the Israelites were near
decisions.reason: Readable says what was shut, and gives the sense of "because of the Israelites": their nearness was the reason.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ רְאֵה֙ נָתַ֣תִּי בְיָֽדְךָ֔ אֶת־יְרִיח֖וֹ וְאֶת־מַלְכָּ֑הּ גִּבּוֹרֵ֖י הֶחָֽיִל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Joshua, see, I have given into your hand Jericho and its king, [the] mighty men of the strength.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "See, I have given into your hand Jericho and its king, the mighty men of valor.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Look, I have handed Jericho over to you, along with its king and its strong warriors.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Look, I have given you Jericho, with its king and its brave soldiers. It is as good as yours.

decisions.choice: I have given: the victory spoken of as already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a finished action, though the city has not yet fallen. God speaks of what he has decided as already settled, as the spies did in 2:24 and the LORD does again in 8:1.

decisions.choice: given into your hand: put in your power
decisions.reason: To give someone into another's hand is to hand them over to that person's control, especially in war (2:24; Deuteronomy 7:24).

decisions.choice: its king, the mighty men of valor: the king together with his warriors
alternatives: its king, mighty men of valor (describing the king and his men together)
decisions.reason: The phrase about the warriors stands beside "its king" with no "and". It most likely adds the king's fighting men to what is handed over; it could also describe the king and his men together. The phrase means men strong and able in battle (1:14).

decisions.choice: the LORD said: the LORD speaks to Joshua, perhaps through the commander of 5:13-15
decisions.reason: Just before this, the commander of the LORD's army has met Joshua and told him to take off his sandals (5:13-15). The commander may be the one who now speaks for the LORD, or the LORD may speak to Joshua directly; the text names only the LORD.

decisions.choice: strong warriors (Balanced); brave soldiers and "It is as good as yours" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give "mighty men of valor" in current words. Readable adds a short sentence to carry the sense of the finished verb (m1): the city is certain to be Israel's.

source.text: וְסַבֹּתֶ֣ם אֶת־הָעִ֗יר כֹּ֚ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה הַקֵּ֥יף אֶת־הָעִ֖יר פַּ֣עַם אֶחָ֑ת כֹּ֥ה תַעֲשֶׂ֖ה שֵׁ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will go around the city, all [the] men of the war, circling the city one time; thus you will do six days.

en.L: And you shall go around the city, all the men of war, circling the city one time. Thus you shall do [for] six days.
en.B: All your fighting men are to march around the city, going around it once. Do this for six days.
en.R: March around the city once with all your soldiers. Do this every day for six days.

decisions.choice: you shall go around, all the men of war: the whole army marches
decisions.reason: The verb "you shall go around" is plural, and "all the men of war" names who "you" are: the whole fighting force, not Joshua alone. The next command, "thus you shall do", is singular, spoken to Joshua as the leader of them all.

decisions.choice: go around ... circling: a procession around the walls
decisions.reason: Two verbs of going around describe the march that fills the chapter. It is a procession around the city, not an attack on its walls.

decisions.choice: march around
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "march", the plain sense of an army going around a city in order; Literal keeps "go around".

source.text: וְשִׁבְעָ֣ה כֹהֲנִ֡ים יִשְׂאוּ֩ שִׁבְעָ֨ה שׁוֹפְר֤וֹת הַיּֽוֹבְלִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָאָר֔וֹן וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י תָּסֹ֥בּוּ אֶת־הָעִ֖יר שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֑ים וְהַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים יִתְקְע֖וּ בַּשּׁוֹפָרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And seven priests will carry seven trumpets of the rams' horns before the ark; and on the day the seventh you will go around the city seven times, and the priests will blow on the trumpets.

en.L: And seven priests shall carry seven trumpets of the rams' horns before the ark. And on the seventh day you shall go around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow on the trumpets.
en.B: Seven priests are to carry seven rams' horns in front of the ark. On the seventh day you are to march around the city seven times, with the priests blowing the horns.
en.R: Have seven priests carry seven trumpets made from rams' horns. They will walk in front of the ark. On the seventh day you must all march seven times around the city, and the priests will blow the trumpets.

decisions.choice: trumpets of the rams' horns: horns of rams, blown as signals
decisions.reason: The instrument is the ram's horn blown to give a signal, not the metal trumpets of Numbers 10:2. The second word also gives its name to the year of jubilee, which such a horn announced (Leviticus 25:9-10); here it names the ram whose horn it is (Exodus 19:13).

decisions.choice: seven: a pattern of completeness
decisions.reason: Seven runs through the account: seven priests, seven horns, seven days, and seven circuits on the seventh day. In Scripture seven often marks a whole that God has set apart (Genesis 2:2-3; Leviticus 25:8). The pattern shows the taking of Jericho as a holy act done in God's way, not an ordinary siege.

decisions.choice: the ark: the chest that held the covenant and stood for the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: The ark held the tablets of the covenant and was the sign of the LORD's presence among his people (3:3, 11; Exodus 25:16, 22). With the horns going before it, the procession shows the LORD himself going around the city.

decisions.choice: trumpets of the rams' horns (Literal); rams' horns, then horns (Balanced); trumpets made from rams' horns, then trumpets (Readable)
alternatives: ram's horn at every level, as in Exodus 19
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 27:13, Literal and Readable use the familiar word "trumpet" and Balanced names the instrument, "ram's horn". Where the Hebrew adds "of the rams' horns", every level says what the horns were made of; where it has the first word alone, Literal and Readable say "trumpets" and Balanced "horns". The same choice holds through the chapter.

source.text: וְהָיָ֞ה בִּמְשֹׁ֣ךְ׀בְּקֶ֣רֶן הַיּוֹבֵ֗ל כְּשָׁמְעֲכֶם֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָ֔ר יָרִ֥יעוּ כָל־הָעָ֖ם תְּרוּעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וְנָ֨פְלָ֜ה חוֹמַ֤ת הָעִיר֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יהָ וְעָל֥וּ הָעָ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ נֶגְדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, at blowing long on [the] horn of the ram, at your hearing the sound of the trumpet, will shout all the people a shout great, and will fall the wall of the city under it, and will go up the people, each before him.

en.L: And it shall be, when [they] blow long on the horn of the ram, when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout a great shout, and the wall of the city shall fall down in its place, and the people shall go up, each one straight before him."
en.B: When they sound a long blast on the ram's horn and you hear the sound of the horn, all the people are to give a great shout. Then the city wall will collapse where it stands, and the people will go up into the city, each of them straight ahead."
en.R: When you hear the priests blow one long blast on the trumpet, all the people must shout as loud as they can. Then the city wall will fall down flat, and everyone can go straight into the city from where they stand."

decisions.choice: when you hear: the read form
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text begin this word with a letter meaning "in", while the vowels and the reading tradition give a letter meaning "as". Both mean "when you hear". The pinned data follows the read form. Reviewers should check this against the manuscript notes.

decisions.choice: fall under itself: collapse where it stands
decisions.reason: The wall is said to fall "under it", in its own place: it falls flat and leaves the way open, rather than being broken through at one point. The same words come in verse 20.

decisions.choice: each straight before him: every one straight ahead
decisions.reason: With the wall down there is no gate or breach to look for. Each goes up from where he stands straight into the city (verse 20).

decisions.choice: a great shout: a loud battle cry
decisions.reason: The shout is the loud cry raised by an army as it goes into battle (1 Samuel 17:20, 52). Here the people raise it at God's command, and the victory follows.

decisions.choice: the priests blow (Readable); go up into the city (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names no one who blows the horn; Readable names the priests, from verse 4. Balanced and Readable say where the people go up, from verse 20.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֞א יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בִּן־נוּן֙ אֶל־הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם שְׂא֖וּ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הַבְּרִ֑ית וְשִׁבְעָ֣ה כֹֽהֲנִ֗ים יִשְׂאוּ֙ שִׁבְעָ֤ה שֽׁוֹפְרוֹת֙ יוֹבְלִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Joshua son of Nun to the priests and said to them, lift up [the] ark of the covenant, and seven priests will carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before [the] ark of Yahweh.

en.L: And Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Lift up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: So Joshua son of Nun summoned the priests and said to them, "Lift up the ark of the covenant. Seven priests are to go ahead of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, carrying seven rams' horns."
en.R: So Joshua son of Nun called the priests together. He said, "Pick up the ark of the covenant, the sacred chest. Seven of you must carry seven trumpets made from rams' horns and walk in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: seven priests shall carry: an instruction
decisions.reason: The verb is a future form used as a command, as in verse 4. Joshua passes on the LORD's words to the priests nearly as he received them.

decisions.choice: the ark of the covenant, the ark of the LORD: two names for one ark
decisions.reason: The ark is named by what it holds, the covenant (Deuteronomy 10:1-5), and in the same sentence by whom it belongs to, the LORD. The two names alternate through the chapter.

decisions.choice: the sacred chest
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ark" once in the chapter, as in Numbers 10:33, and keeps the word "ark".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם עִבְר֖וּ וְסֹ֣בּוּ אֶת־הָעִ֑יר וְהֶ֣חָל֔וּץ יַעֲבֹ֕ר לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to the people, pass on and go around the city, and the armed [one] will pass on before [the] ark of Yahweh.

en.L: And he said to the people, "Pass on, and go around the city, and let the armed [men] pass on before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: And he told the people, "Go forward and march around the city, with the armed men going on ahead of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Then he told the people, "Move out and march around the city. The soldiers with weapons must go in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: and he said: the read form
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text read "and they said", as if the leaders passed the order on; the vowels and the reading tradition give "and he said", with Joshua as the speaker, as in verse 6. The pinned data follows the read form. Either way the command is Joshua's. Reviewers should check this against the manuscript notes.

decisions.choice: the armed men: soldiers equipped for battle
decisions.reason: The word means men stripped for action, armed and ready to fight. It is used of the armed men of the eastern tribes who crossed ahead of Israel (4:12-13; Numbers 32:21). Here the singular stands for the whole armed company.

decisions.choice: the armed [men] (Literal); armed men (Balanced); soldiers with weapons (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is one word used for a group. Literal supplies "men" in brackets; Readable says it in plain words.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כֶּאֱמֹ֣ר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ אֶל־הָעָם֒ וְשִׁבְעָ֣ה הַכֹּהֲנִ֡ים נֹשְׂאִים֩ שִׁבְעָ֨ה שׁוֹפְר֤וֹת הַיּֽוֹבְלִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עָבְר֕וּ וְתָקְע֖וּ בַּשּֽׁוֹפָר֑וֹת וַֽאֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה הֹלֵ֖ךְ אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as had spoken Joshua to the people, and seven the priests carrying seven trumpets of the rams' horns before Yahweh passed on and blew on the trumpets, and [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh going after them.

en.L: And it was, when Joshua had spoken to the people, that the seven priests carrying seven trumpets of the rams' horns before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} passed on and blew on the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was going after them.
en.B: As soon as Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven rams' horns before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went forward blowing the horns, with the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} coming after them.
en.R: As soon as Joshua had given the order, the seven priests started out. They blew their trumpets as they walked ahead of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came along behind them.

decisions.choice: before the LORD: in front of the ark, where the LORD is present
decisions.reason: Where verse 6 says "before the ark of the LORD", this verse says "before the LORD". The ark is so closely bound to the LORD's presence that to go ahead of it is to go ahead of him (Numbers 10:35-36).

decisions.choice: passed on and blew: they set out sounding the horns
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe one movement: the priests went forward and sounded the horns as they went.

decisions.choice: had given the order
decisions.reason: Readable says what Joshua's speaking was: the order of verses 6-7.

source.text: וְהֶחָל֣וּץ הֹלֵ֔ךְ לִפְנֵי֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים תֹּקְעֵ֖י הַשּֽׁוֹפָר֑וֹת וְהַֽמְאַסֵּ֗ף הֹלֵךְ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י הָאָר֔וֹן הָל֖וֹךְ וְתָק֥וֹעַ בַּשּׁוֹפָרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And the armed [one] going before the priests blowing the trumpets, and the rear guard going after the ark, going and blowing on the trumpets.

en.L: And the armed [men] were going before the priests who were blowing the trumpets, and the rear guard was going after the ark, going on and blowing on the trumpets.
en.B: The armed men went on ahead of the priests who were sounding the horns, and the rear guard came behind the ark, with the horns sounding without a break.
en.R: The soldiers with weapons went in front of the priests who were blowing the trumpets. Another group of soldiers followed behind the ark. All the time they marched, the trumpets kept on sounding.

decisions.choice: who were blowing: the read form
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text can be read "they blew", while the vowels and the reading tradition give "blowing". The sense is the same. The pinned data follows the read form. Reviewers should check this against the manuscript notes.

decisions.choice: the rear guard: the troops who close the column
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "gather": the company at the back that keeps the column together and guards it from behind. Numbers 10:25 uses it of the tribe of Dan, the rear guard of all the camps.

decisions.choice: going and blowing: the horns sounded all the way around
decisions.reason: Two verb forms with no stated subject describe action that went on without a break. The ones blowing are the priests (verses 4, 8). The point is that the horns sounded the whole time, while the people kept silent (verse 10).

decisions.choice: Another group of soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says who the rear guard were in plain words.

source.text: וְאֶת־הָעָם֩ צִוָּ֨ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹ֤א תָרִ֨יעוּ֙ וְלֹֽא־תַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ אֶת־קוֹלְכֶ֔ם וְלֹא־יֵצֵ֥א מִפִּיכֶ֖ם דָּבָ֑ר עַ֠ד י֣וֹם אָמְרִ֧י אֲלֵיכֶ֛ם הָרִ֖יעוּ וַהֲרִיעֹתֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [as for] the people, commanded Joshua saying, not you will shout and not you will make heard your voice, and not will go out from your mouth a word, until [the] day I say to you, shout; and you will shout.

en.L: And Joshua commanded the people, saying, "You shall not shout, and you shall not let your voice be heard, and a word shall not go out of your mouth, until the day I say to you, 'Shout!' Then you shall shout."
en.B: Joshua had given the people this order: "Do not shout. Do not let your voices be heard. Not a word is to leave your mouths until the day I tell you, 'Shout!' Then you will shout."
en.R: Joshua had told the people, "Do not shout. Do not make any noise. Do not say a single word until the day I tell you to shout. Then you must shout!"

decisions.choice: the people Joshua commanded: an order already given
decisions.reason: The sentence puts "the people" first, which marks a step aside from the march. It tells what Joshua had ordered the people to do as they went.

decisions.choice: silence until the shout: the people wait for God's signal
decisions.reason: Three commands in a row forbid any noise: no shout, no voice, not a word. For six days the only sound is the horns before the ark. The people's part is to obey and wait for the moment God has set (verse 16).

decisions.choice: had given ... this order (Balanced); had told (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the order stands behind the march already under way (m1). Readable gives Joshua's "Shout!" as reported speech.

source.text: וַיַּסֵּ֤ב אֲרוֹן־יְהוָה֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר הַקֵּ֖ף פַּ֣עַם אֶחָ֑ת וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he caused to go around [the] ark of Yahweh the city, circling one time; and they came [to] the camp and they spent the night in the camp.

en.L: And he made the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} go around the city, circling [it] one time. And they came [into] the camp and spent the night in the camp.
en.B: So he had the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} taken around the city, circling it once. Then they came back to the camp and spent the night there.
en.R: So Joshua had the priests carry the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} around the city one time. Then everyone went back to the camp and stayed there for the night.

decisions.choice: he made the ark go around: Joshua had it carried around
decisions.reason: The verb is causative, "he made go around". The subject is Joshua, who gave the orders; the priests carried the ark (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the camp: Israel's camp at Gilgal
decisions.reason: Israel was camped at Gilgal, east of Jericho (4:19; 5:10). Each day's march ended back in the camp.

decisions.choice: Joshua had the priests carry; everyone
decisions.reason: Readable names who gave the order and who carried the ark (m1), and who went back to the camp.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֥ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose early Joshua in the morning, and lifted the priests [the] ark of Yahweh.

en.L: And Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests lifted up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Joshua got up early the next morning, and the priests took up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Early the next morning Joshua got up, and the priests picked up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} again.

decisions.choice: rose early in the morning: set out at first light, ready to act
decisions.reason: The phrase marks readiness and prompt obedience (3:1; Genesis 22:3). This is the morning of the second day (verse 14).

decisions.choice: the next morning; again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that this is the following day; Readable adds "again".

source.text: וְשִׁבְעָ֣ה הַכֹּהֲנִ֡ים נֹשְׂאִים֩ שִׁבְעָ֨ה שׁוֹפְר֜וֹת הַיֹּבְלִ֗ים לִפְנֵי֙ אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה הֹלְכִ֣ים הָל֔וֹךְ וְתָקְע֖וּ בַּשּׁוֹפָר֑וֹת וְהֶחָלוּץ֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וְהַֽמְאַסֵּ֗ף הֹלֵךְ֙ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה הָל֖וֹךְ וְתָק֥וֹעַ בַּשּׁוֹפָרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And seven the priests carrying seven trumpets of the rams' horns before [the] ark of Yahweh [were] going, going, and they blew on the trumpets; and the armed [one] going before them, and the rear guard going after [the] ark of Yahweh, going and blowing on the trumpets.

en.L: And the seven priests carrying seven trumpets of the rams' horns before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} were going on steadily, and they blew on the trumpets; and the armed [men] were going before them, and the rear guard was going after the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, going on and blowing on the trumpets.
en.B: The seven priests carrying the seven rams' horns went on in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, blowing the horns as they walked. The armed men went ahead of them, and the rear guard came behind the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with the horns sounding without a break.
en.R: The seven priests with trumpets walked in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, blowing their trumpets as they went. The soldiers with weapons went ahead of them, and the other soldiers followed behind the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. All the time they marched, the trumpets kept on sounding.

decisions.choice: going: the read form
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text can be read as another form of the same verb, "going"; the vowels and the reading tradition give the form used in verse 9. The sense is the same. The pinned data follows the read form. Reviewers should check this against the manuscript notes.

decisions.choice: going on steadily ... going and blowing: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: The order of march on the second day is told again in nearly the same words as the first day (verses 8-9): the armed men, the priests with the horns, the ark, the rear guard, and the horns sounding the whole way.

source.text: וַיָּסֹ֨בּוּ אֶת־הָעִ֜יר בַּיּ֤וֹם הַשֵּׁנִי֙ פַּ֣עַם אַחַ֔ת וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה כֹּ֥ה עָשׂ֖וּ שֵׁ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went around the city on the day the second one time and returned [to] the camp; thus they did six days.

en.L: And they went around the city on the second day one time, and returned [to] the camp. Thus they did [for] six days.
en.B: On the second day they marched around the city once and went back to the camp. They did this for six days.
en.R: On the second day they marched around the city one time and went back to the camp. They did the same thing for six days.

decisions.choice: thus they did six days: the march repeated each day through the sixth
decisions.reason: The verse sums up the second to the sixth days: one circuit a day and back to camp, just as the LORD had commanded in verse 3.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וַיַּשְׁכִּ֨מוּ֙ כַּעֲל֣וֹת הַשַּׁ֔חַר וַיָּסֹ֧בּוּ אֶת־הָעִ֛יר כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט הַזֶּ֖ה שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֑ים רַ֚ק בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא סָבְב֥וּ אֶת־הָעִ֖יר שֶׁ֥בַע פְּעָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on the day the seventh, and they rose early at [the] coming up of the dawn and went around the city according to the manner the this seven times; only on the day the that they went around the city seven times.

en.L: And it was on the seventh day, and they rose early, at the coming up of the dawn, and went around the city in this same manner seven times. Only on that day did they go around the city seven times.
en.B: On the seventh day they got up at daybreak and marched around the city in the same way, but this time seven times. That was the only day they went around the city seven times.
en.R: On the seventh day they got up at dawn. They marched around the city the same way as before, but this time they went around seven times. This was the only day they did that.

decisions.choice: in this manner: in the same order of march
decisions.reason: The word means a set way or pattern. The procession was the same as on the six days before, with priests, horns, ark and armed men in their places; only the number of circuits changed.

decisions.choice: only on that day: the seventh day stands apart
decisions.reason: The repeated words stress that this day was unlike the others, as verse 4 had commanded.

decisions.choice: but this time
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the change from the earlier days, which the Hebrew shows by repeating "seven times".

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ בַּפַּ֣עַם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔ית תָּקְע֥וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים בַּשּׁוֹפָר֑וֹת וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אֶל־הָעָם֙ הָרִ֔יעוּ כִּֽי־נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was at the time the seventh, blew the priests on the trumpets, and said Joshua to the people, shout, for has given Yahweh to you the city.

en.L: And it was at the seventh time, [when] the priests blew on the trumpets, that Joshua said to the people, "Shout! For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you the city.
en.B: The seventh time around, when the priests sounded the horns, Joshua said to the people, "Shout! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has handed the city over to you.
en.R: On the seventh time around, the priests blew their trumpets, and Joshua told the people, "Shout! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given you the city!

decisions.choice: shout, for the LORD has given you the city: a shout of trust
decisions.reason: The reason for the shout is that the LORD has already given the city (verse 2). The people shout before they see the wall fall; the shout answers God's promise rather than breaking the wall by its own force.

decisions.choice: has handed the city over to you
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the wording of verse 2 for the same verb, "give" in the sense of handing over in war.

decisions.choice: "Shout!" followed by a second sentence, without "for"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word "for" gives the reason for the command. Balanced and Readable set the reason as its own short sentence after the order, which keeps the link clear without the word. Literal keeps "For".

source.text: וְהָיְתָ֨ה הָעִ֥יר חֵ֛רֶם הִ֥יא וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖הּ לַֽיהוָ֑ה רַק֩ רָחָ֨ב הַזּוֹנָ֜ה תִּֽחְיֶ֗ה הִ֚יא וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתָּ֣הּ בַּבַּ֔יִת כִּ֣י הֶחְבְּאַ֔תָה אֶת־הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁלָֽחְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be the city a devoted thing, it and all that [is] in it, to Yahweh; only Rahab the prostitute will live, she and all who [are] with her in the house, for she hid the messengers whom we sent.

en.L: And the city shall be a devoted thing, it and all that [is] in it, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, she and all who [are] with her in the house, because she hid the messengers whom we sent.
en.B: The city and everything in it are to be devoted to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute is to be spared, she and everyone with her in her house, because she hid the messengers we sent.
en.R: The city and everything in it must be destroyed completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Only Rahab the prostitute and the people with her in her house will be allowed to live, because she hid the spies we sent.

decisions.choice: a devoted thing: given wholly to the LORD, to be destroyed
decisions.reason: The noun is the one explained at Deuteronomy 7:2: something taken out of human use and handed over to the LORD for good, never to be bought back (Leviticus 27:28-29). For a city of the land it means that its people are put to death and nothing is kept for private gain; its metal goods go to the LORD's treasury instead (verse 19).

decisions.choice: and the city shall be: Joshua's words go on through verse 19
decisions.reason: The verb form joins this verse to Joshua's "Shout!" in verse 16, so the rules for the devoted city belong to the same speech. Coming just before the people go in, they set out what the people must keep once they enter the city.

decisions.choice: the prostitute: a woman who sold sex
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a prostitute (2:1). The New Testament remembers Rahab by the same title as an example of faith and of faith shown in action (Hebrews 11:31; James 2:25).

decisions.choice: Rahab is spared: one household excepted from the ban
decisions.reason: In the middle of the command to devote the whole city, one household is excepted, because Rahab sided with Israel and its God (2:9-13). The oath the spies swore to her (2:12-14) binds Israel even within the ban.

decisions.choice: destroyed completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the term in plain words, as at Deuteronomy 7:2. Literal says "a devoted thing" and Balanced "devoted to the LORD for destruction".

decisions.choice: the spies we sent
decisions.reason: The "messengers" are the two spies of chapter 2. Readable says so.

source.text: וְרַק־אַתֶּם֙ שִׁמְר֣וּ מִן־הַחֵ֔רֶם פֶּֽן־תַּחֲרִ֖ימוּ וּלְקַחְתֶּ֣ם מִן־הַחֵ֑רֶם וְשַׂמְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־מַחֲנֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְחֵ֔רֶם וַעֲכַרְתֶּ֖ם אוֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And only you, keep [yourselves] from the devoted thing, lest you devote [it] and take from the devoted thing, and make [the] camp of Israel a devoted thing and trouble it.

en.L: But you, only keep [yourselves] from the devoted thing, lest you devote [it] and take from the devoted thing, and make the camp of Israel a devoted thing and bring trouble on it.
en.B: But as for you, keep away from the things devoted to destruction. Do not devote them and then take any of them for yourselves. If you do, you will make the camp of Israel something devoted to destruction, and you will bring trouble on it.
en.R: But you must stay away from everything that is given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to be destroyed. Do not take any of it for yourselves. If you do, the whole camp of Israel will be given over to destruction, and you will bring trouble on it.

decisions.choice: lest you devote it and take: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "lest you devote [it] and take": having given the things over to the LORD, Israel must not then take them back. The ancient Greek translation reads "lest you covet and take", the words Achan uses in 7:21 ("I coveted them and took them"); the two Hebrew words look much alike. This translation follows the Hebrew. The warning is the same either way: what is devoted may not be taken.

decisions.choice: make the camp a devoted thing: bring the ban on Israel itself
decisions.reason: Whoever takes what is devoted becomes devoted along with it (Deuteronomy 7:26), and the guilt reaches the whole camp. Chapter 7 shows this happen: one man's theft brings defeat on Israel and death on his household.

decisions.choice: bring trouble: the word behind the Valley of Achor
decisions.reason: The verb means to stir up trouble or bring disaster. It comes back when Joshua asks Achan why he has troubled Israel and says the LORD will trouble him, and the place is named the Valley of Achor, "trouble" (7:25-26).

decisions.choice: Do not devote them and then take (Balanced); Do not take any of it (Readable); something devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out the order of the two verbs; Readable keeps only the point, that nothing devoted may be taken. Balanced and Readable say "devoted to destruction" or "given over to destruction" for the camp, as for the city (verse 17). Readable says "given over to the LORD to be destroyed" for the devoted things, the plain sense of the term used at verse 17.

source.text: וְכֹ֣ל׀כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֗ב וּכְלֵ֤י נְחֹ֨שֶׁת֙ וּבַרְזֶ֔ל קֹ֥דֶשׁ ה֖וּא לַֽיהוָ֑ה אוֹצַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה יָבֽוֹא׃

records.literal_gloss: And all silver and gold and articles of bronze and iron, holy it [is] to Yahweh; [the] treasury of Yahweh it will go [into].

en.L: And all silver and gold, and articles of bronze and iron, it [is] holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it shall go into the treasury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: All the silver and gold and everything made of bronze and iron is holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It must go into {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s treasury."
en.R: All the silver and gold and all the things made of bronze and iron are holy and belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They must go into {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s treasury."

decisions.choice: holy to the LORD: set apart as the LORD's own
decisions.reason: Metal goods that fire cannot destroy are not burned but given to the LORD (Numbers 31:22-23, 54). They are still devoted, and no one may keep them for himself (verse 18).

decisions.choice: the treasury of the LORD: the sanctuary's store
decisions.reason: The treasury held what was given to the LORD for his sanctuary (verse 24; compare Exodus 38:24). At this time the sanctuary was the tent of meeting.

decisions.choice: are holy and belong to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "holy" and adds what it means here: these things are the LORD's.

source.text: וַיָּ֣רַע הָעָ֔ם וַֽיִּתְקְע֖וּ בַּשֹּֽׁפָר֑וֹת וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ הָעָ֜ם אֶת־ק֣וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָ֗ר וַיָּרִ֤יעוּ הָעָם֙ תְּרוּעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַתִּפֹּ֨ל הַֽחוֹמָ֜ה תַּחְתֶּ֗יהָ וַיַּ֨עַל הָעָ֤ם הָעִ֨ירָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ נֶגְדּ֔וֹ וַֽיִּלְכְּד֖וּ אֶת־הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And shouted the people, and they blew on the trumpets; and it was, as heard the people the sound of the trumpet, and shouted the people a shout great, and fell the wall under it, and went up the people into the city, each before him, and they captured the city.

en.L: And the people shouted, and they blew on the trumpets. And it was, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, that the people shouted a great shout, and the wall fell down in its place, and the people went up into the city, each one straight before him, and they captured the city.
en.B: So the people shouted, and the horns were blown. As soon as the people heard the sound of the horn, they raised a great shout, and the wall collapsed where it stood. The people went up into the city, each of them straight ahead, and they took the city.
en.R: The priests blew the trumpets, and the people shouted. When the people heard the trumpets, they gave a very loud shout, and the wall of the city fell down flat. Then everyone went straight into the city and captured it.

decisions.choice: the people shouted, and they blew: a summary, then the detail
decisions.reason: The verse first sums up what happened and then tells it step by step: the horns sounded, the people heard and gave the great shout, and the wall fell. It need not mean that the people shouted before the horns, which would go against the order of verses 5 and 16.

decisions.choice: the wall fell: the LORD's doing
decisions.reason: No siege works, ram or ladders are used. The wall falls at the shout the LORD commanded, as he had said it would (verse 5). Hebrews 11:30 says the walls fell by faith, after the people had gone around them for seven days.

decisions.choice: fell under itself; each straight before him: as in verse 5
decisions.reason: The wall falls flat where it stands, and each one goes straight in from where he is.

decisions.choice: The priests blew the trumpets, and the people shouted
decisions.reason: Readable tells the events in the order they happened (m1) and names the priests as those who blew, from verse 16.

source.text: וַֽיַּחֲרִ֨ימוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּעִ֔יר מֵאִישׁ֙ וְעַד־אִשָּׁ֔ה מִנַּ֖עַר וְעַד־זָקֵ֑ן וְעַ֨ד שׁ֥וֹר וָשֶׂ֛ה וַחֲמ֖וֹר לְפִי־חָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they devoted to destruction all that [was] in the city, from man and to woman, from young and to old, and to ox and sheep and donkey, to [the] mouth of [the] sword.

en.L: And they devoted to destruction all that [was] in the city, from man to woman, from young to old, and to ox and sheep and donkey, by the edge of [the] sword.
en.B: They devoted to destruction everything in the city: men and women, young and old, and cattle, sheep and donkeys too. They put them all to the sword.
en.R: They destroyed everything in the city completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. With their swords they killed the men and women, the young and the old, and even the cattle, sheep and donkeys.

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction: as in verse 17
decisions.reason: The verb goes with the noun "devoted thing" of verses 17-18 (see Deuteronomy 7:2): the city's people and animals were killed as given over to the LORD, and nothing was taken as plunder.

decisions.choice: by the mouth of the sword: with the sword, sparing no one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the sword's "mouth", the edge that devours. The phrase means killing with the sword in battle (8:24; Deuteronomy 13:16).

decisions.choice: from man to woman ...: every one, of every kind
decisions.reason: Pairs of opposites, man and woman, young and old, and then the animals, are a way of saying "all": no one was left out, except Rahab's household (verses 22-25).

decisions.choice: the destruction of Jericho: the ban commanded in Deuteronomy 7:2
decisions.reason: This is the command of Deuteronomy 7:2 and 20:16-18 carried out on the first city of the land, and the decision at Deuteronomy 7:2 gives its limits and its reasons. It is bound to the peoples of this land and to the danger that they would turn Israel to other gods, and the land's wrongs, not Israel's goodness, are named as its ground (Deuteronomy 9:4-5; Genesis 15:16). The chapter itself shows the ban's edges: a Canaanite household that turned to Israel's God is spared (verse 25), and the next chapter shows an Israelite who takes what is devoted falling under the ban himself (7:1, 24-26). The verse reports what was done; it does not by itself settle how the strong language of war in these accounts is to be weighed.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, Readable gives the sense of the term in plain words; Literal and Balanced keep "devoted to destruction". "With their swords they killed" gives the idiom of m2 plainly.

source.text: וְלִשְׁנַ֨יִם הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים הַֽמְרַגְּלִ֤ים אֶת־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ בֹּ֖אוּ בֵּית־הָאִשָּׁ֣ה הַזּוֹנָ֑ה וְהוֹצִ֨יאוּ מִשָּׁ֤ם אֶת־הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לָ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּעְתֶּ֖ם לָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to [the] two the men who spied out the land said Joshua, go [into the] house of the woman the prostitute and bring out from there the woman and all who [belong] to her, as you swore to her.

en.L: And to the two men who had spied out the land Joshua said, "Go into the house of the woman, the prostitute, and bring out from there the woman and all who [belong] to her, as you swore to her."
en.B: Joshua gave an order to the two men who had spied out the land: "Go to the prostitute's house and bring out the woman and everyone who belongs to her, just as you promised her with an oath."
en.R: Joshua told the two men who had gone to spy on the land, "Go to the house of Rahab the prostitute. Bring her out, and everyone who belongs to her, just as you promised her with an oath."

decisions.choice: as you swore to her: the spies' oath of chapter 2
decisions.reason: The two spies had sworn to spare Rahab and her family if she kept their errand secret and if her family stayed inside her house, marked by the red cord in the window (2:12-21). Joshua now has Israel keep that oath.

decisions.choice: all who belong to her: her household
decisions.reason: The phrase covers the people of her house and may take in what they owned. Verse 23 names her father, mother and brothers and the rest of her family.

decisions.choice: to the two men ... Joshua said: the hearers named first
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with the two spies, turning the story from the city's fall to them and to Rahab.

decisions.choice: Rahab (Readable); promised her with an oath (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names the woman, from verse 17. "Promised with an oath" keeps the force of "swore".

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ הַנְּעָרִ֣ים הַֽמְרַגְּלִ֗ים וַיֹּצִ֡יאוּ אֶת־רָ֠חָב וְאֶת־אָבִ֨יהָ וְאֶת־אִמָּ֤הּ וְאֶת־אַחֶ֨יהָ֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לָ֔הּ וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־מִשְׁפְּחוֹתֶ֖יהָ הוֹצִ֑יאוּ וַיַּ֨נִּיח֔וּם מִח֖וּץ לְמַחֲנֵ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And went the young men the spies and brought out Rahab and her father and her mother and her brothers and all who [belonged] to her; and all her clans they brought out, and set them outside of [the] camp of Israel.

en.L: And the young men, the spies, went in and brought out Rahab and her father and her mother and her brothers and all who [belonged] to her; and they brought out all her clans and set them outside the camp of Israel.
en.B: So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, with her father and mother, her brothers, and all who belonged to her. They brought out all her relatives and settled them outside the camp of Israel.
en.R: So the two young spies went in and brought Rahab out, together with her father and mother, her brothers, and everyone else who belonged to her. They brought out her whole family and gave them a place to stay outside the camp of Israel.

decisions.choice: the young men: the two spies
decisions.reason: The word for a young man is also used of a trusted helper; Joshua himself is called Moses' young man (Exodus 33:11).

decisions.choice: all her clans: her whole wider family
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a clan, a wide family group. With "all" in the plural it means every relative who had gathered in her house, as the spies had told her to do (2:18).

decisions.choice: outside the camp: not yet part of Israel
decisions.reason: The camp was to be kept holy because the LORD walked among his people there (Deuteronomy 23:15). Rahab's family were outsiders who had not yet joined the people of the covenant, and they were most likely placed outside the camp for that reason. Verse 25 says she went on to live among Israel.

decisions.choice: relatives (Balanced); whole family (Readable); settled them, gave them a place to stay
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "clans". Balanced and Readable use words for family that fit one household's relatives, and say what setting them outside the camp involved.

source.text: וְהָעִ֛יר שָׂרְפ֥וּ בָאֵ֖שׁ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֑הּ רַ֣ק׀הַכֶּ֣סֶף וְהַזָּהָ֗ב וּכְלֵ֤י הַנְּחֹ֨שֶׁת֙ וְהַבַּרְזֶ֔ל נָתְנ֖וּ אוֹצַ֥ר בֵּית־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the city they burned with fire and all that [was] in it; only the silver and the gold and the articles of the bronze and the iron they put [into the] treasury of [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And the city they burned with fire, and all that [was] in it; only the silver and the gold and the articles of bronze and iron they put into the treasury of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then they burned the city with fire, and everything in it. But they put the silver and gold and the bronze and iron goods into the treasury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house.
en.R: Then they burned the city and everything in it. But they took the silver, the gold, and the things made of bronze and iron, and put them in the treasury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house.

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD: the LORD's sanctuary, at this time the tent
decisions.reason: There was no temple yet. "The house of the LORD" can name the sanctuary of any period, as in Exodus 23:19 and 34:26; here it is the tent of meeting and its store (verse 19).

decisions.choice: they burned the city: nothing kept for gain
decisions.reason: Burning the city with all its goods carries out the ban of verse 17. Only what was given to the LORD's treasury was saved (verse 19), so no one in Israel grew rich from Jericho's fall. Deuteronomy 13:17 commands the same for an Israelite town that turns to other gods.

source.text: וְֽאֶת־רָחָ֣ב הַ֠זּוֹנָה וְאֶת־בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֤יהָ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לָהּ֙ הֶחֱיָ֣ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ בְּקֶ֣רֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֤י הֶחְבִּ֨יאָה֙ אֶת־הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לְרַגֵּ֥ל אֶת־יְרִיחֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Rahab the prostitute and [the] house of her father and all who [belonged] to her let live Joshua, and she has lived in [the] midst of Israel until the day the this, for she hid the messengers whom sent Joshua to spy out Jericho.

en.L: But Rahab the prostitute and the house of her father and all who [belonged] to her Joshua kept alive, and she has lived in the midst of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.
en.B: But Joshua spared the life of Rahab the prostitute, along with her father's household and everyone who belonged to her, and she has lived among the people of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers Joshua had sent to spy out Jericho.
en.R: But Joshua let Rahab the prostitute live, along with her father's family and everyone who belonged to her. She has lived among the people of Israel to this day. This was because she hid the men Joshua had sent to spy on Jericho.

decisions.choice: kept alive: spared from death
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative of "live": Joshua let her live, as he had commanded in verse 17.

decisions.choice: she has lived ... to this day: down to the writer's own time
decisions.reason: The phrase speaks from the time the account was written and says that Rahab's family went on living in Israel (compare 4:9; 5:9). "She" may mean Rahab herself or her household after her.

decisions.choice: Rahab in later Scripture
decisions.reason: Matthew 1:5 names Rahab among the ancestors of King David and of Jesus, and Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25 point to her as a woman of faith. The outsider spared from the city became part of Israel's own line.

decisions.choice: among the people of Israel; the men Joshua had sent
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people of Israel" for "the midst of Israel"; Readable says "the men" for the messengers, as in verse 17.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁבַּ֣ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖יא לֵאמֹ֑ר אָר֨וּר הָאִ֜ישׁ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָקוּם֙ וּבָנָ֞ה אֶת־הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ אֶת־יְרִיח֔וֹ בִּבְכֹר֣וֹ יְיַסְּדֶ֔נָּה וּבִצְעִיר֖וֹ יַצִּ֥יב דְּלָתֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And made swear Joshua at the time the that, saying, cursed [be] the man before Yahweh who rises and builds the city the this, Jericho; with his firstborn he will lay its foundation, and with his youngest he will set up its gates.

en.L: And Joshua made [them] swear at that time, saying, \q "Cursed [be] the man before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who rises up and builds this city, Jericho! \q With his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, \q and with his youngest he shall set up its gates."
en.B: At that time Joshua put the people under this oath: \q "Cursed before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be the man who sets out to rebuild this city, Jericho! \q At the price of his firstborn he will lay its foundation; \q at the price of his youngest he will set its gates in place."
en.R: At that time Joshua made the people take this oath: \q "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} curse the man who tries to build this city of Jericho again! \q His oldest son will die when he lays its foundation. \q His youngest son will die when he puts up its gates."

decisions.choice: made them swear: put the people under an oath
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative of "swear". Joshua bound the people by an oath that the city would not be rebuilt, and the oath takes the form of a curse on whoever does it. It may also mean that Joshua himself spoke a solemn oath.

decisions.choice: cursed before the LORD: under a curse the LORD will carry out
decisions.reason: A curse spoken "before the LORD" calls on him to enforce it (Deuteronomy 27:15-26). The words are set out in two matching lines, the firstborn with the foundation and the youngest with the gates.

decisions.choice: with his firstborn ... with his youngest: at the cost of his sons
decisions.reason: The little word "with" here gives the price paid: the builder will lose his eldest son when the work begins and his youngest when it is finished. The foundation and the gates are the first and last parts of building a walled city.

decisions.choice: fulfilled in 1 Kings 16:34
decisions.reason: In the days of King Ahab, Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho. He laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram his firstborn and set up its gates at the cost of Segub his youngest, according to the word the LORD had spoken through Joshua son of Nun (1 Kings 16:34). The curse falls on rebuilding Jericho as a fortified city; the place is still named as a town of Benjamin and is lived in at times before Hiel (18:21; Judges 3:13; 2 Samuel 10:5).

decisions.choice: May the LORD curse ...; His oldest son will die when ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns "cursed before the LORD" into a prayer that the LORD act, and says plainly what "with his firstborn" means (m3, as 1 Kings 16:34 shows).

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "them" in brackets; Balanced and Readable name the people as those put under the oath (m1).

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ וַיְהִ֥י שָׁמְע֖וֹ בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was Yahweh with Joshua, and was his fame in all the land.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joshua, and his fame was in all the land.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joshua, and his fame spread through the whole land.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joshua, and people everywhere in the land heard about him.

decisions.choice: the LORD was with Joshua: the promise of 1:5 kept
decisions.reason: The LORD had promised Joshua, "As I was with Moses, I will be with you" (1:5, 9; 3:7). The fall of Jericho shows that promise kept.

decisions.choice: his fame: the report of him
decisions.reason: The word means what is heard about someone. News of Joshua, and of the LORD who was with him, spread through the land, as news of the crossing had (5:1; 9:1-3).

decisions.choice: people everywhere in the land heard about him
decisions.reason: Readable turns the noun "fame" into a plain sentence.
